title: Gracebanded credit slabs, emergency reallocation and late invoice refund rules
creator: Aisha Rao
description: PRD for introducing a ‘gracebanded credit slab’ model for plans, an emergency reallocation flow for transient overages, and clear rules for late invoice refunds. The goal is to reduce support tickets for small overages, provide predictable behavior for bursty workloads, and automate common reconciliations to save finance/ops time.
background: Customers frequently hit short-lived usage spikes (prefix caching warmups, batch jobs, CI runs) that create low-dollar overages and generate high-touch billing tickets. Current approaches (hard overage charges or manual credits) are inconsistent across plans. Finance and Customer Support have requested a deterministic, auditable mechanism that (1) absorbs tiny bursts without invoices, (2) enables controlled emergency credit reallocation for critical customers, and (3) standardizes late invoice refund policies to reduce dispute cycles.
goals: Establish credit slab tiers per plan that auto-absorb small transient overages (gracebanding)
Provide a documented emergency reallocation process usable by CS/RevOps with audit logs and limits
Define late invoice refund SLAs and edge-case rules that can be enforced by billing automation
Minimize manual reconciliation work and billing disputes by 30% in Q2
non_goals: Rewrite core billing metering; we will build on top of existing metering snapshots
Offer unlimited forgiveness — gracebands are for small transient overages only
Change pricing tiers or plan feature entitlements in this project
requirements: R1: Per-plan configuration: graceband percent (e.g., 2%), slab absolute cap (e.g., $25/month), and reset cadence (monthly) must be configurable
R2: Automatic absorption: when a customer’s overage for a billing window <= slab cap, do not generate an invoice line item; mark usage as ‘absorbed-by-graceband’
R3: Emergency reallocation: allow CS/RevOps to move unused committed credits from one paying entity to another within the same organization up to a per-org monthly limit with two-person approval
R4: Audit trail: every automated absorption and manual reallocation must produce an immutable record (who, why, amount, invocation id) surfaced in Console and exported to the billing ledger
R5: Refund rules: late invoice refund requests must be auto-evaluated against eligibility criteria (age <= 60 days, amount <= $200 or < 5% of invoice total) and either auto-apply or route to RevOps
R6: Opt-out: enterprise customers can opt-out of graceband absorption at the org level
R7: Telemetry: emit metrics for absorbed_count, absorbed_amount, reallocations_count, reallocations_amount, refund_auto_applied_count, refund_routed_count
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Console shows per-org graceband config; when enabled, test tenant with synthetic usage that would otherwise produce a $15 overage shows zero invoice delta and an 'absorbed' ledger entry

AC-2: Reallocation workflow in Console requires two distinct approvers, records the approver IDs and a reason string, and results in adjusted credit balances visible in the org ledger within 10 minutes
AC-3: Automated refund decisions match decision-table in PRD for 1,000 historical invoices in test dataset with >= 98% fidelity
AC-4: Audit export to S3/BigQuery contains at least the fields: timestamp, actor, action_type, amount_usd, original_invoice_id, reason, run_id
AC-5: Default plan configs for gracebanding applied to all paid plans and documented in Billing policy page
AC-6: No increase in invoice generation latency > 500ms (p95) for customers with high-concurrency metering during billing run
AC-7: Metrics pipeline surfaces absorbed_amount and reallocations_amount to Finance dashboard with <5 minute latency
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'gracebanding' for billing service; 2) Internal dogfood on Redwood-Internal org with manually seeded configs for two weeks; 3) Enable for 10% of paid plans selected by revops (low-risk customers) and monitor metrics + tickets for 2 billing cycles; 4) Gradual ramp to 100% after sign-off. Emergency reallocation UI gated behind RBAC (RevOps role) and requires 2FA. Refund automation launched as 'assist' mode (suggest + apply with revops approval) then flipped to 'auto' after 30 days and 95% precision on test set.
